title: CI/CD Security, OIDC, and Artifact Attestations Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies ci/cd security, oidc, and artifact attestations?
options: Concentrate short-lived release authority in protected jobs and bind provenance to final artifact digests.
Pin actions to mutable tags only
questions.answer: Concentrate short-lived release authority in protected jobs and bind provenance to final artifact digests.
questions.explanation: This answer preserves the underlying platform or delivery contract while requiring representative evidence, explicit failure behaviour, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: GitHub id-token write grants repository contents write permission.
questions.explanation: Giving id-token write to all jobs and trusting only the repository name lets compromised or unintended workflows request powerful cloud identities.

questions.prompt: What security property does OIDC improve over a stored cloud key?
questions.answer: It issues short-lived, claim-bound credentials without keeping a long-lived cloud secret in GitHub.
questions.explanation: The response identifies the mechanism that makes the decision reliable instead of relying on a convenient proxy.
